newsitem.title: USA: Florida sinkhole threatens frozen food king's home.
newsitem.headline: Florida sinkhole threatens frozen food king's home.

text.p: Sunken living rooms are making a comeback -- at least in one Florida mansion.

A mansion belonging to a frozen food king became the latest sinkhold victim when a maid discovered the living room floor sank about a foot (0.4 metre) overnight, fire department officials said on Tuesday. Pillars were left dangling in thin air and menaced a valuable art collection.

The enclave of Heathrow, home to many multi-million dollar mansions, is in a part of central Florida known for marshy depressions or sinkholes that open overnight, swallowing cars, schools, even homes.
Now one is working on the palatial estate built by Gino Paulucci, founder of Chung King and Gino's Pizza.
A live-in housekeeper discovered the living room had sunk overnight, leaving pillars dangling over cracked terra-cotta tiles. The depression was about 15 feet (4.6 metres) in diameter.
The Seminole County Fire Department was called in to rescue works of art valued at more than a million dollars, said Ken Roberts, spokesman for the Seminole County Public Safety Department.

"Right now it looks as if its stabilised somewhat, but its very difficult to tell," Roberts said. "Sinkholes can open quickly then grow very slowly. Engineers will be out there tomorrow to look it over and see if the house can be saved."
Paulucci developed the entire Heathrow community in the 1980s. His office said he had no comment.
